articles.title: Anthropic Sets a Price Range for Its Huge Stock Market Debut
articles.easyKo: 클로드를 만든 앤트로픽이 주식 시장에 처음 상장하려고 주식 값의 범위를 정했어요. 최대 기업 가치는 약 1조 4천억 달러로, 한 번에 최대 644억 달러를 모을 수 있어요. 투자자들이 AI에 아직 돈을 걸 마음이 있는지 보여 주는 시험대로 봐요.

paragraphs.en: Anthropic, the company that makes the Claude chatbot, has set a price range for its first public share sale. It plans to sell 825 million shares at 70 to 78 dollars each. At the top of that range, the company would be worth about 1.4 trillion dollars. That number counts stock options and similar securities. The sale could raise up to 64.4 billion dollars.
paragraphs.ko: 클로드 챗봇을 만드는 앤트로픽이 처음으로 주식을 일반에 파는 값의 범위를 정했어요. 회사는 주식 8억 2,500만 주를 한 주에 70달러에서 78달러에 팔 계획이에요. 그 범위의 맨 위 값이면 회사 가치는 약 1조 4천억 달러가 돼요. 이 숫자에는 스톡옵션과 비슷한 증권도 들어 있어요. 이번 판매로 최대 644억 달러를 모을 수 있어요.

The company was last valued at 965 billion dollars in a private funding round. The shares are expected to trade on the Nasdaq under the symbol ANT. The BBC reports that trading will start on 19 November.

But the company has promised almost 900 billion dollars for computing with partners such as Amazon and Google.

paragraphs.en: Many people see the sale as a test of how much investors still trust AI companies. The company's filing also warns about competition, safety and security risks. articles.title: Trump Says the War in Iran Is 'Effectively Over' as Oil Prices Fall

Qatar's prime minister met Trump at the White House on Monday. But Trump kept a naval blockade in place, and he said US forces are ready to act if things change. He gave no sign of pulling back the thousands of US troops sent near Iran. In earlier months, Trump often threatened bigger attacks and then backed down.

paragraphs.en: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4 percent in October from September, the Labor Department said on Tuesday. That is faster than forecasters expected, because analysts had predicted a rise of 0.3 percent. The monthly rise in September was larger, at 0.6 percent.

paragraphs.en: Housing costs made up more than 30 percent of the October increase. Food prices went up 0.5 percent, and grocery prices rose sharply. Energy prices rose 0.7 percent, much less than the 5.2 percent jump in September.
paragraphs.ko: 주거 관련 비용이 10월 상승분의 30% 넘게 차지했어요. 식료품 값은 0.5% 올랐고, 장바구니 물가가 크게 뛰었어요. 에너지 값은 0.7% 올랐는데, 9월의 5.2% 급등보다 훨씬 적었어요.

paragraphs.en: This report has no yearly number for inflation. The reason is last year's government shutdown, so officials never recorded prices for October 2025. Before the report, the Cleveland Federal Reserve Bank estimated that prices were up 3.7 percent from a year ago. Average wages grew only 3.1 percent in the same time, so the typical worker is losing buying power.
paragraphs.ko: 이번 보고서에는 연간 물가 상승률 수치가 없어요. 작년 정부 업무 정지 때문에 2025년 10월 물가를 기록하지 못했기 때문이에요. 보고서가 나오기 전에 클리블랜드 연방준비은행은 물가가 1년 전보다 3.7% 올랐다고 추정했어요. 같은 기간 평균 임금은 3.1%만 올라서 보통 노동자의 구매력은 줄고 있어요.

paragraphs.en: Gasoline gave some relief to drivers. The national average price fell below $4 a gallon on Tuesday for the first time in three months, according to AAA. Regular gas now costs $3.98, which is 38 cents lower than a month ago. It is still a record high for this time of year, about a dollar above the price when the U.S. went to war with Iran. A GasBuddy analyst, Patrick De Haan, said the average could reach $3.75 by Thanksgiving if nothing surprising happens.
paragraphs.ko: 휘발유 값은 운전자들에게 다소 숨통을 틔워 줬어요. 미국자동차협회에 따르면 전국 평균 가격은 화요일에 석 달 만에 갤런당 4달러 밑으로 내려갔어요. 일반 휘발유는 지금 3.98달러로 한 달 전보다 38센트 쌌어요. 그래도 이맘때로는 사상 최고 수준이고, 미국이 이란과 전쟁을 시작했을 때보다 약 1달러 높아요. 가스버디의 분석가 패트릭 드 한은 큰 돌발 상황이 없으면 추수감사절쯤 평균이 3.75달러까지 내려갈 수 있다고 말했어요.

paragraphs.en: The numbers matter for interest rates. Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said before the report that energy shocks may have longer effects on inflation than people thought. The BBC reported that he was leaning toward a rate increase in December. Analysts say the higher-than-expected October number makes a rate rise at the Fed's December meeting more likely. The Fed's goal is to keep yearly inflation at 2 percent.

articles.title: Ukraine and Russia Hold a Constructive First Day of Talks
articles.easyKo: 러시아와 우크라이나가 미국의 중재로 아부다비에서 첫날 회담을 했어요. 4시간쯤 이어졌고 젤렌스키 대통령은 건설적이었다고 말했어요. 하지만 동부 지역 문제로 두 나라의 입장은 아직 멀어요.

paragraphs.en: Russia and Ukraine held their first day of peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. The United States is helping to run the talks. The meeting lasted nearly four hours. It is the first such meeting since February. The war has lasted nearly five years, and analysts say it has killed hundreds of thousands of soldiers.

paragraphs.en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky was not in the room. He called the talks constructive and substantive. He said the sides also discussed prisoner exchanges. Zelensky said the talks mostly covered humanitarian issues, such as returning civilians and children taken from Ukraine. Security guarantees were also discussed. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the meeting very productive, but he said there is a lot of work to do.

The BBC says the chain is on the brink of collapse.

talk.answer: I think we should read it carefully. The study found a link between bone drugs and lower dementia risk. But it was an observational study, so it cannot prove cause. I would wait for more research before changing any treatment.
talk.answerKo: 조심스럽게 읽어야 한다고 생각해요. 연구는 뼈 약과 낮은 치매 위험 사이의 연관을 찾았어요. 하지만 관찰 연구라서 원인을 증명할 수 없어요. 치료를 바꾸기 전에 더 많은 연구를 기다리겠어요.

articles.title: Scientists find a gut-to-brain pathway that helps us learn to like bitter coffee
articles.easyKo: 처음엔 쓴 커피를 나중에 좋아하게 되는 이유의 일부를 과학자들이 찾았어요. 장에서 뇌로 가는 느린 도파민 신호가 맛과 영양을 연결해 줘요. 쥐 실험이 중심이고 사람에게도 비슷한 모습이 보였어요.

paragraphs.en: Black coffee tastes bitter at first, yet many people learn to love it. Scientists at UC San Francisco may now know part of the reason. They found a slow dopamine pathway between the gut and the brain. The study was published on November 4 in Nature.

sents.en: The study was published on November 4 in Nature.

paragraphs.en: Dopamine is a chemical messenger linked to motivation, reward and learning. Most studies look at fast signals that last seconds. This new pathway is slower. It responds to nutrients like sugar and fat after food enters the digestive system, and its signal lasts several minutes.

talk.q: Why do people learn to like foods they first dislike?
talk.qKo: 사람들은 처음 싫던 음식을 왜 좋아하게 될까요?
talk.answer: I think the brain learns from experience. A new study says a slow dopamine signal links taste with the benefits of food. For example, coffee starts to taste better when the brain links it with caffeine. This makes me want to try new foods more than once.
talk.answerKo: 뇌가 경험에서 배운다고 생각해요. 새 연구는 느린 도파민 신호가 맛과 음식의 이로움을 연결한다고 말해요. 예를 들어 뇌가 커피를 카페인과 연결하면 커피가 더 맛있어져요. 그래서 새 음식을 한 번 이상 먹어 보고 싶어져요.
